podcast.body: "Acquiesce" is tucked at the end of the Cigarettes & Alcohol EP (April 24, 1995). One British magazine rated it the second greatest Oasis song of all time, behind only "Live Forever" — ahead of "Supersonic," "Champagne Supernova," and even "Wonderwall." No one has adequately explained why it was not a proper single. It features a rare Liam and Noel Gallagher duet, with Liam sounding more like John Lennon than ever. The timing would have been perfect: Noel had walked out on the band during a US tour in late 1994, generating tabloid coverage for months, and the lyrical content — "we need each other, we believe in each other" — would have carried enormous biographical resonance. It was later collected on the 1998 B-sides compilation The Master Plan. Hardcore fans maintain that you cannot fully understand Oasis without exploring their B-sides, and Oasis has released over three albums' worth of non-album material. "Hardcore fans maintain that you can't understand Oasis completely if you don't get into their B-sides."

podcast.body: Originally a B-side to "Some Might Say," this song, like "Supersonic," came together at the very last minute. In February 1995, Noel Gallagher was traveling by train to Loco studio in Wales when the train broke down in the Severant Tunnel, leaving him stuck for four hours. He overheard a passenger use the word "Aquies" during a phone call, liked the sound, and began strumming the opening chords, working out 90% of the arrangement despite a fellow passenger's protest to stop playing. Liam Gallagher sang the verses, and Noel sang the chorus because Liam, recovering from a throat infection after dates in Japan, couldn't hit the high notes. Alan McGee was so impressed he wanted it as the single, but Noel insisted on "Some Might Say." It eventually gained recognition, promoted as the single for the 1998 compilation "The Masterplan" and also appearing on "Stop the Clocks." "When the song made it to the studio, it was decided that Liam would sing the verses and Noll would take care of the chorus because Liam just couldn't hit those high notes."
